Three principles govern architecture: first single-dispatcher convenience plus per-system specificity. turbulence_sim() accepts system name forwards appropriate integrator. integrator also exists exported function users need direct control system-specific parameters. second explicit deterministic-versus-stochastic flag. simulators carry stochastic argument. text: Edward Lorenz’s 1963 discovery deterministic chaos emerged attempt model atmospheric convection using drastically truncated spectral representation Boussinesq equations [4]. Working MIT numerical weather prediction, Lorenz found simplified three-variable model exhibited behavior later recognized hallmark chaos: bounded non-periodic orbits sensitive dependence initial conditions. story Lorenz discovered sensitivity, re-running simulation slightly rounded initial conditions observing completely different long-term behavior, become legendary history science. system describes motion two-dimensional fluid layer heated , known Rayleigh-Bénard convection. three state variables direct physical interpretations: \(x\) measures rate convective overturning, positive values correspond clockwise circulation convection cell; \(y\) represents horizontal temperature variation across cell, quantifying temperature contrast ascending descending currents; \(z\) captures departure vertical temperature profile linearity, positive values indicating stable stratification conductive state. governing equations : \[\frac{dx}{dt} = \sigma(y - x)\] \[\frac{dy}{dt} = x(\rho - z) - y\] \[\frac{dz}{dt} = xy - \beta z\] parameter \(\sigma\) Prandtl number, ratio kinematic viscosity thermal diffusivity \(\sigma = \nu/\kappa\), determines quickly momentum diffuses relative heat. parameter \(\rho\) Rayleigh number, representing ratio buoyancy viscous forces, serves primary control parameter. \(\rho < 1\), convection occurs heat transferred purely conduction. \(1 < \rho < \rho_c \approx 24.74\) (\(\sigma = 10\), \(\beta = 8/3\)), system exhibits stable steady convection form convection rolls. Beyond critical value, system undergoes subcritical Hopf bifurcation leading chaotic behavior. geometric factor \(\beta = 4/(1 + ^2)\) relates horizontal wave number \(\) convection pattern controls rate energy dissipation vertical mode. standard choice \(\beta = 8/3\) corresponds critical wave number onset convection. canonical parameters \(\sigma = 10\), \(\rho = 28\), \(\beta = 8/3\), system exhibits chaotic behavior strange attractor characteristic butterfly shape. trajectory alternates unpredictably two lobes, representing alternation clockwise counterclockwise convection. bistability irregular switching became paradigmatic example deterministic chaos. Lyapunov spectrum parameters computed high precision [5]: \(\lambda_1 \approx 0.9056\), \(\lambda_2 = 0\), \(\lambda_3 \approx -14.572\). positive largest exponent confirms chaos, nearby trajectories diverging exponentially rate roughly \(e^{0.91t}\). zero exponent reflects continuous time nature flow, large negative third exponent indicates strong dissipation. Kaplan-Yorke dimension, computed \(D_{KY} = 2 + \lambda_1/|\lambda_3| \approx 2.06\), confirms attractor slightly two-dimensional, fractal object embedded three-dimensional phase space. Lorenz strange attractor viewed three-dimensional phase space. butterfly-shaped geometry reflects system’s bistable structure, trajectories spiraling around two unstable fixed points transitioning chaotically wings. package provides tools estimating dynamical invariants directly time series, following methods nonlinear time series analysis developed 1980s 1990s. computing Lyapunov exponents, must determine appropriate embedding dimension using Cao’s method [6], provides practical algorithm identifying reconstructed attractor unfolded true dimension.  theoretical foundation attractor reconstruction Takens’ embedding theorem [7], establishes \(d\)-dimensional attractor, embedding dimension \(n \geq 2d + 1\) generically provides diffeomorphic reconstruction scalar time series. text: Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) process, introduced Leonard Ornstein George Uhlenbeck 1930 [20], emerged need resolve fundamental paradox Brownian motion theory. Einstein’s 1905 model Brownian motion predicted particle’s instantaneous velocity infinite probability one, physically absurd consequence arising non-differentiability Wiener process. Ornstein Uhlenbeck constructed model particle velocity follows well-defined stochastic process, position obtained integration. OU process since become canonical model mean-reverting stochastic phenomena, finding applications across physics, finance, biology, geosciences. context turbulent chaotic dynamical systems, OU process provides mathematically tractable yet physically realistic representation colored (temporally correlated) noise forcing.

title: Turbulent attractors: theory and practice
text: one-dimensional OU process \(X_t\) satisfies stochastic differential equation (SDE): \[dX_t = \phi(\mu - X_t) \, dt + \sigma \, dW_t\] \(\phi > 0\) relaxation rate (inverse timescale), \(\mu\) long-run mean process reverts, \(\sigma > 0\) volatility noise amplitude, \(W_t\) standard Wiener process satisfying \(\mathbb{E}[dW_t] = 0\) \(\mathbb{E}[dW_t^2] = dt\). three parameters clear physical interpretations: Relaxation rate \(\phi\): Controls quickly process returns mean perturbation. characteristic time scale \(\tau = 1/\phi\); larger \(\phi\) means faster mean reversion rapidly decorrelating noise. Mean \(\mu\): equilibrium level around process fluctuates. \(\mu = 0\), noise centered; non-zero \(\mu\) introduces systematic drift bias forcing. Amplitude \(\sigma\): Controls intensity random fluctuations. stationary variance \(\sigma^2/(2\phi)\), standard deviation fluctuations scales \(\sigma/\sqrt{2\phi}\).

title: Turbulent attractors: theory and practice
text: OU process one SDEs admitting closed-form solution. initial condition \(X_0 = x_0\): \[X_t = \mu + (x_0 - \mu)e^{-\phi t} + \sigma \int_0^t e^{-\phi(t-s)} \, dW_s\] first term \(\mu\) deterministic long-run mean; second term \((x_0 - \mu)e^{-\phi t}\) shows exponential decay initial condition; third term stochastic integral representing accumulated noise exponentially fading memory. process Gaussian times, : \[\mathbb{E}[X_t] = \mu + (x_0 - \mu)e^{-\phi t}\] \[\text{Var}(X_t) = \frac{\sigma^2}{2\phi}(1 - e^{-2\phi t})\] \(t \\infty\), process reaches stationary distribution: \[X_\infty \sim \mathcal{N}\left(\mu, \frac{\sigma^2}{2\phi}\right)\] autocorrelation function stationary process : \[\rho(\tau) = \mathbb{E}[(X_t - \mu)(X_{t+\tau} - \mu)] / \text{Var}(X) = e^{-\phi|\tau|}\] exponential decay characteristic first-order Markov process produces Lorentzian power spectrum: \[S(f) = \frac{\sigma^2}{\pi(\phi^2 + 4\pi^2 f^2)}\] spectrum flat (white) low frequencies \(f \ll \phi/(2\pi)\) decays \(1/f^2\) high frequencies, interpolating white noise Brownian motion.

title: Simulate the full 6-mode Charney-DeVore model with bistability — charney_devore_6mode
text: full 6-mode Charney-DeVore equations : $$\dot{x}_1 = -C(x_1 - x_1^*) + \tilde{\gamma}_1 x_3$$ $$\dot{x}_2 = -Cx_2 + \beta_1 x_3 - \alpha_1 x_1 x_3 - \delta_1 x_4 x_6$$ $$\dot{x}_3 = -Cx_3 - \beta_1 x_2 + \alpha_1 x_1 x_2 + \delta_1 x_4 x_5 - \gamma_1 x_1$$ $$\dot{x}_4 = -C(x_4 - x_4^*) + \varepsilon(x_2 x_6 - x_3 x_5) + \tilde{\gamma}_2 x_6$$ $$\dot{x}_5 = -Cx_5 + \beta_2 x_6 - \alpha_2 x_1 x_6 - \delta_2 x_4 x_3$$ $$\dot{x}_6 = -Cx_6 - \beta_2 x_5 + \alpha_2 x_1 x_5 + \delta_2 x_4 x_2 - \gamma_2 x_4$$ derived coefficients (alpha, beta, gamma, delta, epsilon) depend channel geometry (b), planetary vorticity gradient (beta), topographic amplitude (gamma) according spectral truncation formulas Charney DeVore (1979). Unlike simplified 3-mode version, full model can exhibit genuine bistability appropriate parameter regimes. original Charney-DeVore (1979) paper demonstrated specific topographic amplitudes forcing strengths, two stable equilibria coexist: high-index (strong zonal flow, weak waves) low-index (weak zonal flow, amplified waves, blocking) states. Finding bistable regimes requires careful parameter tuning bifurcation analysis; standard parameters produce single stable equilibrium. Stochastic forcing can induce variability intermittent transitions even without deterministic bistability.

F < 1 gives stable zonal flow; F ≈ 1-2 produces multiple equilibria (bistability); F > 2.5 tends toward high-index state . n_steps Number integration steps. dt Time step Euler-Maruyama integration. x0, y0, z0 Initial conditions state variables. x0 = 1 starts near high-index (zonal) state; smaller x0 larger y0, z0 starts closer blocking. k Ekman (frictional) damping coefficient (default 0.1). Represents rate momentum dissipation boundary layer friction: \(k \sim f / (2H)\) f Coriolis parameter H Ekman depth. Higher k stabilizes system favors zonal state. alpha Nonlinear wave-mean flow interaction coefficient (default 1.0). Controls strength triad coupling zonal flow waves. Derived vorticity equation \(\alpha \sim k_w^2\) k_w wavenumber. Larger α enhances nonlinear interactions can destabilize zonal flow. beta Topographic/thermal wave forcing coefficient (default 0.5). Represents external thermal gradient forces planetary waves baroclinic conversion. original model, β related topographic height wavenumber structure. Larger β means stronger wave excitation mean flow gradient. delta Wave-wave (self) interaction coefficient (default 1.0). Controls internal nonlinear coupling wave modes y z. Derived spectral projection advection term. δ affects wave amplitude saturation mechanism. sigma Noise amplitude (default 0.15). Represents unresolved synoptic-scale variability (weather) perturbs large-scale flow. Noise can trigger transitions metastable states. ou_phi Ornstein-Uhlenbeck relaxation rate (default 0.0). φ = 0, white noise used; φ > 0 produces temporally correlated noise decorrelation time 1/φ, representing persistent weather patterns. ou_mu Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process mean (default 0.0). OU process reverts value rate φ. Non-zero μ introduces systematic bias noise forcing, can shift preferred state occupancy. stochastic Logical; TRUE (default), enable stochastic forcing. seed Random seed reproducibility. thin Thinning factor output (store every thin-th point). transient Number initial steps discard transient.

title: Simulate Hasselmann stochastic climate model — hasselmann_sim
text: F_forcing External radiative forcing anomaly (default 0.0). Represents changes planetary energy budget greenhouse gases, solar variability, volcanic aerosols. Positive F represents net warming (e.g., increased CO2); negative F represents cooling. Units non-dimensional, F = 1 corresponds roughly forcing ~3-4 W/m² (approximately 2×CO2). n_steps Number integration steps. dt Time step non-dimensional units (default 0.1). One time unit corresponds approximately thermal relaxation time surface ocean mixed layer (~years decades). climate applications, dt = 0.1 represents sub-decadal resolution. T0 Initial surface temperature anomaly (default 0.0). Positive values indicate warming relative reference climate. Td0 Initial deep ocean temperature anomaly (default 0.0). deep ocean responds much slower surface due large heat capacity. I0 Initial ice extent (default 0.5). Normalized ice coverage = 0 ice-free = 1 maximum glaciation. lambda Climate feedback parameter (default 0.1). aggregate effect fast feedbacks (Planck, water vapor, lapse rate, clouds) surface temperature. Higher λ means stronger negative feedback (faster relaxation equilibrium). Climate sensitivity ∝ 1/λ. gamma Ocean heat uptake coefficient (default 0.05). Controls rate heat exchange surface deep ocean: γ = C_s/(C_d × τ_m) C_s, C_d heat capacities τ_m mixing timescale. Larger γ means faster equilibration surface deep ocean. kappa Deep ocean relaxation rate (default 0.01). Controls quickly deep ocean temperature relaxes toward surface temperature: κ ∝ 1/τ_deep τ_deep deep ocean turnover time (~centuries). Small κ reflects long memory deep ocean. alpha_ice Ice-albedo feedback strength (default 0.1). strongly ice extent affects surface temperature changes planetary albedo. ice-albedo feedback positive: ice → higher albedo → cooling → ice. captured −α×temperature equation. beta_ice Ice dynamics timescale (default 0.02). rate ice extent adjusts toward equilibrium value: β ∝ 1/τ_ice τ_ice ice sheet response time (millennia continental ice sheets, decades sea ice). mu_ice Ice-temperature sensitivity (default 0.5). Slope ice equilibrium curve: I_eq = max(0, −μ×T). Larger μ means ice responds sensitively temperature changes. parameter controls strength ice-albedo feedback loop. sigma_T Temperature noise amplitude (default 0.3). Represents integrated effect high-frequency atmospheric variability (weather) slow climate state. Hasselmann's key insight: weather appears stochastic forcing climate system. sigma_I Ice noise amplitude (default 0.1). Represents stochastic variability ice dynamics factors like precipitation variability, ocean heat transport fluctuations, ice calving events. ou_phi_T, ou_phi_I Ornstein-Uhlenbeck relaxation rates temperature ice noise (defaults 0.0). φ = 0, white noise used; φ > 0 produces temporally correlated (red) noise decorrelation time 1/φ. Red noise better represents persistent atmospheric patterns. ou_mu_T, ou_mu_I Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process means temperature ice noise (defaults 0.0). OU process reverts values rate φ. Non-zero means introduce systematic bias representing long-term forcing. stochastic Logical; TRUE (default), enable stochastic forcing. deterministic version shows underlying attractor structure. seed Random seed reproducibility. thin Thinning factor output (store every thin-th point). transient Number initial steps discard transient.

title: Simulate the Rössler system — rossler_sim
text: Linear feedback parameter controlling spiraling behavior (default 0.2). parameter determines rate trajectories spiral outward x-y plane. Increasing ~0.3 begins period-doubling cascade; ≈ 0.1 gives simple limit cycle. b Offset parameter z-dynamics (default 0.2). Controls baseline excitation z variable. chemical oscillator analogies, b represents constant feed rate reactant. Small changes b limited effect dynamics. c Threshold parameter controlling reinjection mechanism (default 5.7). z exceeds approximately c, z(x - c) term becomes strongly positive, producing rapid excursion reinjects trajectory back toward attractor. primary bifurcation parameter: c < 4 gives periodic orbits; c ≈ 4-6 shows period-doubling; c > 5.7 produces fully developed chaos; c > 12 can produce hyperchaos divergence. n_steps Number integration steps (default 500000). dt = 0.001 thin = 5, gives 500 time units (~80 orbits) 100000 output points. dt Time step RK4 integration (default 0.001). Smaller values give smoother trajectories; Rössler system less stiff Lorenz. x0, y0, z0 Initial conditions. Defaults (1, 1, 0) place trajectory near inner loop attractor. seed Random seed reproducibility. thin Thinning factor output (default 5). every thin-th point stored, reducing memory maintaining smooth visualization. transient Number initial steps discard transient. stochastic Logical; TRUE, add Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noise x-equation, representing external perturbations model uncertainty. noise_phi OU relaxation rate (default 1.0). Higher values give faster-decorrelating noise. noise_sigma OU noise amplitude (default 0.1). noise_mu OU process mean (default 0.0).

title: Simulate the Rössler system — rossler_sim
text: Rössler system designed minimal chaotic flow, simpler Lorenz system exhibiting similar strange attractor dynamics: $$\frac{dx}{dt} = -y - z$$ $$\frac{dy}{dt} = x + ay$$ $$\frac{dz}{dt} = b + z(x - c)$$ Unlike Lorenz two symmetric lobes, Rössler attractor single-band structure: trajectories spiral outward x-y plane z triggers reinjection pulse, creating characteristic "funnel" shape. Physical interpretation: purely mathematical origin, equations can model certain chemical reaction kinetics (e.g., Belousov- Zhabotinsky reaction variants) x y represent oscillating concentrations z represents slowly accumulating inhibitor periodically "fires" reset oscillation. Parameter regimes: c < 3 Simple limit cycle (periodic) c ≈ 3-4 Period-2 orbit c ≈ 4-5 Period-4 higher period orbits (period-doubling cascade) c ≈ 5.7 Onset chaos, standard chaotic parameters c > 12 Risk unbounded growth hyperchaos standard parameters (= 0.2, b = 0.2, c = 5.7), system exhibits strange attractor Lyapunov spectrum approximately \(\lambda_1 \approx 0.07\), \(\lambda_2 = 0\), \(\lambda_3 \approx -5.4\), giving Kaplan-Yorke dimension approximately 2.01, slightly lower Lorenz attractor.

title: Simulate Stommel box model for thermohaline circulation — stommel_sim
text: eta2 Non-dimensional freshwater flux high latitudes (default 1.0). primary bifurcation control parameter, representing rate freshwater input precipitation minus evaporation polar box. \(\eta_2 = E / (\alpha \Delta T^*)\) E freshwater flux \(\Delta T^*\) reference temperature difference. Values 0.8-1.5 span bistable regime thermal haline circulation modes stable. n_steps Number integration steps. dt Time step Euler-Maruyama integration. T0, S0 Initial conditions non-dimensional temperature salinity differences equatorial polar boxes. T0 = 2, S0 = 1 starts thermal circulation regime. eta1 Non-dimensional surface thermal forcing (default 3.0). Represents restoring temperature difference imposed atmosphere-ocean heat flux: \(\eta_1 = T^*_{eq} / \Delta T^*\) \(T^*_{eq}\) equilibrium equator-pole temperature difference. Larger η₁ favors thermal mode. eta3 Ratio thermal haline relaxation timescales (default 0.3). Physically, \(\eta_3 = \tau_T / \tau_S\) τ_T τ_S e-folding times surface temperature salinity anomalies. Since heat exchanges faster salt (τ_T < τ_S), η₃ < 1 realistic oceans. Smaller η₃ makes salinity persistent favors haline circulation. sigma_T, sigma_S Noise amplitudes temperature salinity (defaults 0.2). Represent unresolved atmospheric variability affecting air-sea fluxes. Typical ratio σ_S/σ_T depends whether precipitation temperature variability dominates. ou_phi Ornstein-Uhlenbeck relaxation rate (default 0.0). φ = 0, white noise used; φ > 0 produces temporally correlated (red) noise decorrelation time 1/φ. ou_mu_T, ou_mu_S Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process means temperature salinity noise (defaults 0.0). OU process reverts values rate φ. Non-zero means introduce systematic bias noise forcing. stochastic Logical; TRUE (default), enable stochastic forcing. seed Random seed reproducibility. thin Thinning factor output (store every thin-th point). transient Number initial steps discard transient.

title: Simulate Stommel box model for thermohaline circulation — stommel_sim
text: Object class "stommel_sim" containing: t Time vector (non-dimensional, scaled τ_T) T Temperature difference (equator minus pole), positive = normal gradient S Salinity difference (equator minus pole) q Flow strength q = T - S, proportional density difference. Positive q indicates thermally-driven circulation (like modern Atlantic); negative q indicates salinity-driven (reversed) circulation. parameters List simulation parameters

title: Simulate Stommel box model for thermohaline circulation — stommel_sim
text: non-dimensional Stommel equations : $$\frac{dT}{dt} = \eta_1 - T(1 + |T - S|)$$ $$\frac{dS}{dt} = \eta_2 - S(\eta_3 + |T - S|)$$ stochastic forcing: $$dT = [\eta_1 - T(1 + |q|)] dt + \sigma_T dW_T$$ $$dS = [\eta_2 - S(\eta_3 + |q|)] dt + \sigma_S dW_S$$ \(q = T - S\) flow strength (proportional density difference). model exhibits bistability: certain parameter values, thermally-dominated circulation (\(q > 0\), like modern Atlantic) salinity-dominated circulation (\(q < 0\)) stable. Stochastic forcing can induce transitions states, creating intermittent dynamics reminiscent paleoclimate records.

title: Estimate largest Lyapunov exponent — turbulence_lyapunov
text: largest Lyapunov exponent \(\lambda_1\) quantifies average rate exponential divergence (convergence) nearby trajectories phase space: $$|\delta(t)| \sim |\delta(0)| e^{\lambda_1 t}$$ \(\delta(t)\) represents separation initially close trajectories time \(t\). positive exponent (\(\lambda_1 > 0\)) indicates deterministic chaos sensitive dependence initial conditions; trajectories diverge exponentially, making long-term prediction impossible despite underlying determinism. Negative exponents indicate asymptotically stable behavior perturbations decay, zero exponents characterize marginally stable systems limit cycles. Wolf algorithm (1985): original method Lyapunov estimation experimental data. algorithm tracks single fiducial trajectory nearest neighbor reconstructed phase space. separation exceeds threshold (max_scale), current neighbor replaced new one lying within epsilon fiducial point, maintaining similar orientation. exponent computed : $$\lambda_1 = \frac{1}{t_M} \sum_{k=1}^{M} \log_2 \frac{L'(t_k)}{L(t_{k-1})}$$ \(L(t_k)\) \(L'(t_k)\) distances replacement. Wolf method robust computationally intensive requires careful parameter tuning. evolve_steps parameter controls many time steps pass potential neighbor replacements. Rosenstein algorithm (1993): simpler, faster method particularly suitable small datasets. point trajectory, algorithm finds nearest neighbor (temporal separation exceeding theiler_window avoid correlated neighbors) tracks divergence time. mean logarithmic divergence computed across reference points: $$S(k) = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{j=1}^{N} \ln d_j(k)$$ \(d_j(k)\) distance \(j\)-th pair neighbors \(k\) time steps. Lyapunov exponent estimated slope linear region \(S(k)\) versus \(k\). max_steps parameter controls maximum divergence time tracked. method produces divergence curve can visualized plot(). Method selection: Use "rosenstein" exploratory analysis visualization divergence behavior; faster produces interpretable diagnostics. Use "wolf" comparison historical literature values, remains standard reference algorithm. methods require adequate embedding dimension (embed_dim) determined via turbulence_cao appropriate time delay (tau). Reference Lyapunov exponents systems standard parameters: Lorenz (\(\sigma\)=10, \(\rho\)=28, \(\beta\)=8/3): \(\lambda_1 \approx 0.906\) Rössler (=0.2, b=0.2, c=5.7): \(\lambda_1 \approx 0.07\) Lorenz-84 (=0.25, b=4, F=8, G=1): \(\lambda_1 \approx 0.07\) vonkarman (\(\mu\)=0.3): \(\lambda_1 \approx 0.02-0.1\) charney_devore: typically positive multistable stommel/hasselmann: may negative (stable) near zero

title: tuRbulence 0.1.0
text: Lorenz system (lorenz_sim()): atmospheric convection model butterfly attractor; reference Lyapunov exponent λ₁ ≈ 0.906 Rössler system (rossler_sim()): single-scroll attractor studying period-doubling routes chaos; reference λ₁ ≈ 0.07 Lorenz-84 (lorenz84_sim()): low-order atmospheric model capturing westerly wind eddy interactions
